[whispers] Now, the move I promised. In early 2026, he shipped an MCP server, a CLI and an API, so AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT can post for you. In his words: "My revenue just exploded once I started sending to agents." He moved the product to where demand was going.

topic: Business breakdown: Postiz — Postiz is the ultimate agentic social media scheduler tool

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Postiz — Postiz is the ultimate agentic social media scheduler tool
pick.angle: A solo open-source dev built a social media scheduler that now makes $370K, by giving the code away for free

research.what_it_does: An open-source, agentic social media scheduler. You plan, generate and schedule posts across many networks. It has an MCP server, CLI and API, so AI agents like Claude or ChatGPT can post for you.
research.who_pays: Creators, small brands, agencies and developers or automation teams. They pay for the hosted cloud version instead of self-hosting.
research.pricing: Official pricing page, monthly billing: Standard $29, Team $39, Pro $49, Ultimate $99 per month. Annual billing is $23, $31, $39 and $79 per month (about 20% off). Every plan has a 7-day free trial ('Start for $0'). Every plan includes the MCP server, CLI and API. Standard is marked 'No team support'. Self-hosting is free.
growth: Nevo's first instinct was SEO: he hired an Upwork freelancer to buy backlinks and write articles. He then went open source instead (via a thread by Saurav on X, a secondary source: https://x.com/saguppa/status/2038972079094038712).

Postiz launched on September 1, 2024. It reached almost 14k GitHub stars, #1 Product of the Day, Week and Month on Product Hunt, 584K Docker downloads and almost 4,000 cloud registrations (same X thread, secondary source).

Indie Hackers write-up of Nevo's account: Postiz was the first good open-source social scheduler, and every release was published on r/selfhosted. Everything is organic with no ads. Nevo also ran 4 Product Hunt launches (https://www.indiehackers.com/post/tech/growing-an-open-source-product-to-1-3m-arr-in-two-years-hbMiXIoZsueV9D3L58DP).

Daily.dev summary of Nevo's talk: launch posts on r/selfhosted and similar communities each reached at least 200,000 views with no existing audience. He also pushed for GitHub trending status. Paid quote-repost networks and creator collaborations on X now sustain over 100K views per post (https://daily.dev/posts/the-marketing-playbook-behind-a-207k-month-saas-nevo-david-from-postiz-7w7e75jlr).

Pivot to AI agents: in early 2026 Nevo shipped an agent CLI, an MCP server, a ClawHub skill and programmatic landing pages when OpenClaw exploded (Super Frameworks, secondary source). Mixergy interview headline: 'Revenue jumped when he sold to AI agents'. The same X thread quotes him: 'My revenue just exploded once I started sending to agents.'

Per the Creative Chaos newsletter (secondary, citing a founder interview): a user's article about using Postiz with an open-source AI agent got 7.2 million views on X, and trials jumped to roughly 700 per day. Nevo then copied the format with his own article (about 500,000 views) and paid for reposts (about $60–$350 each, about 20 per article). The newsletter says churn fell from the mid-to-high 20% range to 13.7%.
founder_story: Nevo David spent nearly seven years as an engineer. Several failed startups left him in debt (Sofarbot, a secondary source). He joined open-source notification company Novu in 2022 as a growth marketer to learn distribution (Sofarbot; Super Frameworks says he drove that repo to 30,000 GitHub stars in two years).
His first product, Gitroom, was an open-source launch-planning tool that went live in March 2024. After about six months he judged the market too small and expanded it into Postiz (Sofarbot).

Described as a solo, bootstrapped founder for years (Best Million Startups, Super Frameworks, Saurav's X thread). Indie Hackers: 'After many failed startups' he built Postiz and reached $1.3M ARR in two years.
lessons: Use open source as free top-of-funnel. The GitHub repo, r/selfhosted posts and Product Hunt gave a pre-revenue product an audience. The hosted cloud version then monetises people who don't want to run servers.
Reposition to where demand is moving. Postiz went from a human-dashboard scheduler to the publishing layer for AI agents (MCP, CLI, API). Per Nevo's own account, revenue jumped after that.
When a format or story is already winning attention, copy the format and then pay to amplify it. Postiz did this with the OpenClaw article, per the Creative Chaos newsletter.
criticism: It is a crowded category. Saurav's X thread says there are 1,000+ competitors and that Hootsuite has been around since 2008. Cheaper rivals exist (e.g. Social Champ, PostFast, Socialync).

Churn has been high. Nevo cited 17% monthly churn in early 2026, and one article says it was in the mid-to-high 20% range before it fell to 13.7%. Subscriber growth depends on constantly bringing in new customers.
The product is free to self-host. Cloud customers pay for convenience, and Meta and YouTube API approvals can take over a month for self-hosters (Socialync).
Revenue is not profit. No cost or profit data was found. Early 'founder statements' on revenue are not audits (Sofarbot).
Some growth leans on a hype cycle (OpenClaw, MCP, agentic AI). That wave could fade.
facts: Self-hosted version runs the same codebase as the paid cloud product (Atticus Li, secondary).

Postiz repo had about 35,300 GitHub stars, 6,700 forks and 80 contributors, and its container package passed 7.5 million downloads. These are distribution indicators, not user counts (Steal What Works, about 67 days old).
Postiz is AGPL-3.0 licensed per PostFast; Super Frameworks says Apache 2.0, so verify on GitHub before stating a license.

Early MRR milestones (secondary): about $700 a few months before Jan 2025, then $2K MRR in Jan 2025 with about 15K stars. Super Frameworks says $17K MRR from 472 paying subscribers. Saurav's thread (about 218 days old) says over $45K MRR, up 3x since Jan 2026.
Indie Hackers: $1.3M ARR in two years.
Mixergy lists 'Larry', an OpenClaw agent, as co-writer of an article that helped drive Postiz's growth.
Systemaic (secondary): the brand name 'postiz' alone gets about 85,520 monthly searches.
do_not_claim: Profit, margins or team size today. Sources say 'solo for years', but TrustMRR and Best Million Startups mention reinvesting in hiring, so don't say it's still solo.
That Postiz is 'no ads'. The Indie Hackers post says everything is organic, but paid quote-reposts on X are reported later.
Exact GitHub star count or license. Figures vary by source (14K, 25K, 30K, 33K, 34K, 35K) and the license is AGPL-3.0 vs Apache 2.0.
The pricing page lists unlimited posts, while a homepage FAQ reportedly says 400 posts per month on Standard (Filip Konecny review). Don't state a post limit.
That the OpenClaw viral article numbers (7.2M views, 700 trials/day) are first-party. They come from a newsletter citing a founder interview.
Any claim that open source plus an AI trend guarantees similar results.
Older third-party MRR figures ($17K, $45K, $170K, $194K) are stale. Use only the TrustMRR numbers for current revenue.
research.notes: The pricing page text was retrieved by search. Check the exact on-screen text when recording (e.g. whether it shows '$29/mo' or '$29'). Most growth details are from secondary sources (X threads, newsletters, write-ups). Attribute them as 'per Nevo's own account' or similar, and don't present them as audited. Dates are exact: Gitroom went live in March 2024, Postiz launched September 1, 2024, and TrustMRR lists the founding as July 2024, a small discrepancy. Revenue figures in the reel should come only from TrustMRR (MRR $369,751, 10,864 active subscriptions).
